Prithviraj Chauhan: King of Ajmer from 1177 to 1192.
Blinded in one eye by childhood smallpox, he fought his first battle at ten and went on to found the Sikh Empire, capturing Lahore and ruling as its first maharaja. Who was he?
This member of a famous political dynasty spent decades in environmental law before becoming a high-profile anti-vaccine activist—and in 2025 took a Cabinet role. Who?
Robert F. Kennedy Jr.: American politician (born 1954)
SPONGE: Political pressure group. Its founder and first President was reported to be named James "Sandy" McMenemon.
A philosopher who held a chair in comparative religion at Calcutta before entering public life, this scholar rose from Vice President to President of India in 1962 — who was he?
Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan: President of India from 1962 to 1967. Radhakrishnan's philosophy was grounded in Advaita Vedanta, reinterpreting this tradition for a contemporary understanding.
In Hinduism, what name is given to the feminine 'Universal Power' that complements Shiva and is worshipped at shrines called pithas?
Shakti: Divine feminine energy in Hinduism.
Born in 1955, this Princess Royal of Thailand is the second daughter of King Bhumibol Adulyadej and the younger sister of King Vajiralongkorn — who is she?
Sirindhorn: Thai princess (born 1955). Maha Chakri Sirindhorn, The Princess Royal (born 2 April 1955) is a member of the Thai royal family.
His was the longest reign of any Ottoman sultan, taking Belgrade in 1521 and Rhodes in 1522 and shattering Hungary's army at Mohács in 1526 — who was this sultan?
Suleiman the Magnificent: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (1520–1566)
Also called the Decalogue, these covenant directives were given to Moses atop Mount Sinai and later smashed after he found the Israelites worshipping a golden calf. What are they?
Ten Commandments: Biblical principles relating to ethics and worship.
Ten days before the 1968 Summer Olympics opened as scheduled, Mexican armed forces opened fire on unarmed student protesters in a Mexico City plaza — what is this event called?
Tlatelolco massacre: 1968 killing of anti-government protestors by the Mexican Armed Forces in Mexico City.
Head of state for nearly 26 years and often called an autocrat, this longest-serving Finnish president steered a policy of "active neutrality." Who was he?
Urho Kekkonen: President of Finland from 1956 to 1982.
Canonized as a saint by both the Catholic and Orthodox churches, this Rurik dynasty ruler seized Kiev with a Varangian army in 978 after his brothers' deadly feud — who is he?
Vladimir the Great: Grand Prince of Kiev from 978 to 1015.
Crowned King of Prussia in 1861, this Hohenzollern monarch became the first emperor of a unified Germany a decade later — who was he?
Wilhelm I: German Emperor from 1871 to 1888.
Known by his initials, this Indian politician served as chief minister of Andhra Pradesh for two terms before dying in a 2009 helicopter crash over a forest — who was he?
Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy: Chief minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Yeduguri Sandinti Rajasekhara Reddy (8 July 1949 – 2 September 2009), popularly known as YSR, was an Indian politician.
From Chittagong in March 1971 he broadcast his nation's declaration of independence; he later rose to become its sixth president and is remembered there as the 'Martyr President.' Which leader?
Ziaur Rahman: President of Bangladesh from 1977 to 1981.
Who among these was born first?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
William Osler (born 1849) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these is a physicist?
Max von Laue is a physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Alfred Nobel is a chemist. Alfred Bernhard Nobel ( noh-BEL; Swedish: [ˈǎlːfrɛd nʊˈbɛlː]; 21 October 1833 – 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.
What is the atomic number of Einsteinium?
Einsteinium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Es and atomic number 99 and is a member of the actinide series and the seventh transuranium element.
In what year was Hamish Harding born?
Hamish Harding: George Hamish Livingston Harding (24 June 1964 – 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
In what year was Vikram Sarabhai born?
Vikram Sarabhai: Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
In what year was Johann Wolfgang von Goethe born?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year did Aryabhata die?
Aryabhata: The claim that Nalanda used to be located in Kusamapura/Pataliputra also cannot be proven.
In what year did Ivan Pavlov die?
Ivan Pavlov: Pavlov also conducted significant research on the physiology of digestion, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1904.
In what year was Iodine discovered?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
In what year was Nickel discovered?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Magnesium sulfate: Pfizer. It is a white crystalline solid, soluble in water.
In which country is Fish and chips?
Fish and chips: United Kingdom. Fish and chips is a hot dish consisting of battered and fried fish, served with chips.
Who is credited with discovering Norma?

Norma (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is Latin for normal, referring to a right angle, and is variously considered to represent a rule, a carpenter's square, a set square or a level.
Who is credited with discovering Aspartame?
Aspartame: James M. Schlatter. Aspartame is an artificial, non-saccharide sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.
Who is credited with discovering Histamine?
Histamine: Henry Hallett Dale. Histamine or histamin is an organic nitrogenous compound found in mammals and many vegetables, fruits and food products.
About 5 million tonnes of acetic acid are produced annually largely to make this compound, most commonly in polymer form — what is it?
Acetate is a salt formed by the combination of acetic acid with a base (e.g. sodium hydroxide), an ester of acetic acid, or the anion CH3COO- found in solution.
First approved in the United States in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor treats high uric acid levels linked to gout, kidney stones, and chemotherapy — what medication is it?
Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
This symptom, not a diagnosis by itself, refers to a loss of appetite in humans and — under the name 'inappetence' — in animals from dogs to goats. Which symptom?
Anorexia (symptom) is a medical term for a loss of appetite.
The second-largest living lizard species after the Komodo dragon, native to South and Southeast Asia. It's a varanid found from India to the Indonesian islands. What is it?
Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
Causing frequent urination and a weak stream, this noncancerous enlargement of a male gland isn't caused by poor hygiene and has no known cure, only symptom management. What condition is it?
Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), also called prostate enlargement, is a noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland.
Belonging to the Colubridae family of venomous snakes and found only in Sub-Saharan Africa, this reptile's scientific name is Dispholidus typus — what is it commonly called?
Boomslang (or; Dispholidus typus) is a highly venomous snake in the family Colubridae.
This American actress is remembered chiefly as the mother of a famous Hollywood actress and actor, and the former wife of actor Jon Voight. Who is she?
Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
Named for the whisker-like barbels many species sport, these scaleless ray-finned fish include some of the largest freshwater giants in Southeast Asia and Eurasia — name this diverse group of fish?
Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).
This insect family, known as the 'true' members of its group, contains roughly 3,400 species worldwide, distinct from just two species in a smaller sister family. What family is it?

Cicadidae is one of two families of cicadas, with about 3,400 species in over 520 genera worldwide; it contains most living cicada species, except for the two belonging to its sister taxon, the Tettigarctidae.

Serving as personal doctor to a superstar singer on the day of his 2009 death, this physician was later convicted of involuntary manslaughter over the misuse of a surgical anesthetic as a sleep aid — who is he?
Conrad Murray (born February 19, 1953) is a Grenadian-born American former physician convicted for his role in the death of American singer and dancer Michael Jackson.
Unrelated to poor hygiene, this scalp condition causes flaking and mild itching and is often treated with antifungal or keratolytic remedies; about half of all adults experience it. What is it?
Dandruff is a skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
Made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice, this thin South Indian bread is traditionally served with chutney and sambar — what is it?

Dosa (food) (in Indian English) or thosai (in Malaysian English and Singapore English) is a thin, savoury batter bread in South Indian cuisine made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice.
The tallest native bird in Australia and the third-tallest living bird overall, this flightless ratite can grow up to 1.9 metres tall. What bird is it?
Emu (Dromaius novaehollandiae) is a species of flightless bird endemic to Australia, where it is the tallest native bird.
Equivalent to one coulomb per volt, this SI unit of electrical capacitance is named after a pioneering English physicist — name the unit?
Farad (symbol: F) is the unit of electrical capacitance, the ability of a body to store an electrical charge, in the International System of Units (SI), equivalent to 1 coulomb per volt (C/V).
Having led Renault, Sauber, and Alfa Romeo's F1 outfits, this French engineer took the reins at Ferrari as team principal in 2023 — who is he?
Fred Vasseur (French; born 28 May 1968) is a French motorsport executive, businessman and engineer.
This pancreatic hormone kicks in when blood sugar dips too low, prompting the liver to convert stored glycogen back into glucose. What is it?
Glucagon is a peptide hormone, produced by alpha cells of the pancreas.
This Austrian physician wrote over 300 publications and termed his diagnosis of autism 'autistic psychopathy,' though later allegations tied him to a Nazi-era clinic in Vienna — what was his name?
Hans Asperger (18 February 1906 - 21 October 1980) was an Austrian physician.
Which cosmological relationship says a galaxy's recession speed is proportional to its distance from Earth, discovered via redshift measurements and usually credited to a 1929 paper?
Hubble's law is the observation in physical cosmology that galaxies are moving away from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance.
This post-transition metal, chemically similar to gallium and thallium, was identified spectroscopically in 1863 and takes its name from the indigo line in its spectrum — what element is it?
Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Born in Albuquerque and a Princeton engineering graduate, this businessman founded and once ran Amazon, the e-commerce and cloud-computing giant — who is he?

Jeff Bezos (n Jorgensen; born January 12, 1964) is an American businessman, and the founder, executive chairman, and former president and CEO of Amazon, the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company.
Also called a kilopond, this deprecated gravitational metric unit equals exactly 9.80665 newtons — the weight of a one-thousand-gram mass under standard gravity. What is it?
Kilogram-force (kgf or kgF), or kilopond (kp, from Latin pondus, 'weight'), is a non-standard gravitational metric unit of force equal to the weight on Earth of a one-kilogram mass.
This leafy member of the daisy family is eaten raw in salads and sandwiches, though one Asian variety, celtuce, is grown instead for its edible stem — what is it?
Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) is an annual plant of the family Asteraceae mostly grown as a leaf vegetable.
Often caused by cigarette smoking or inhaled chemicals damaging airway cell DNA, this malignant tumor often shows no symptoms until it has already spread. What disease is it?
Lung cancer is a malignant tumor that originates in the tissues of the lungs.
Working on the geometry of Riemann surfaces, this Tehran-born Stanford professor became in 2014 the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal — who was she?
Maryam Mirzakhani (12 May 1977 - 14 July 2017) was an Iranian mathematician and a professor of mathematics at Stanford University.

Introduced in 1975 and still in production today at two Russian factories, this Soviet-designed helicopter family serves as both a medium twin-turbine transport and, in gunship form, an armed attack aircraft — what's the helicopter?

Mil Mi-17 (NATO reporting name: Hip) is a Soviet-designed Russian military helicopter family introduced in 1975 (Mi-8M), continuing in production as of 2024 at two factories in Russia, in Kazan and Ulan-Ude.

This symbiotic relationship between a fungus and a plant, in which fungal threads interconnect with plant roots at the cellular level, plays a major role in plant nutrition and soil chemistry — what is it called?
Sold in packs needing a desiccant to keep it from absorbing moisture, this seaweed sheet was once used as currency and shrine offerings in Japan — what is it?
Nori is a dried edible seaweed used in Japanese cuisine, usually made from species of the red algae genus Pyropia, including P. yezoensis and P. tenera.
Often linked to polycystic ovary syndrome or pelvic inflammatory disease, this fluid-filled sac can cause severe pain if it ruptures or twists — what is it?
Ovarian cyst is a fluid-filled sac within the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
Listed in the Dictionary of Fungi as containing over 300 species, this mold genus produces a compound that stops bacterial growth and also flavors certain cheeses — which genus?
Penicillium is a genus of ascomycetous fungi that is part of the mycobiome of many species and is of major importance in the natural environment, in food spoilage, and in food and drug production.
This scientific term for a group of fin-footed, mostly marine mammals includes walruses, sea lions, fur seals, and true earless seals — 34 living species in all. What is the term?
Pinniped are a widely distributed and diverse clade of carnivorous, fin-footed, semiaquatic, mostly marine mammals.
Lacking any real scientific definition, this British term for a large swimming crustacean has become almost interchangeable with 'shrimp' — what is it?
Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (members of the order of decapods), some of which are edible.

This small herbivore belongs to the family Leporidae alongside hares, and the European species of its genus has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what bouncy little prey animal is it?
Rabbit are small mammals in the family Leporidae (which also includes the hares), which is in the order Lagomorpha (which also includes pikas).

This English mathematical physicist shared a 1988 Wolf Prize with Stephen Hawking, won a 2020 Nobel for black-hole work, and dreamed up an 'impossible' triangle that inspired M. C. Escher — who is he?
Roger Penrose (born 8 August 1931) is an English mathematician, mathematical physicist, and philosopher of science.
Before becoming a full-time cartoonist in 1995, this creator of a hit workplace-satire comic strip worked various corporate jobs — who is he?
Scott Adams (June 8, 1957 - January 13, 2026) was an American cartoonist, author, and commentator.
This mammal family is known for its warning coloration and its ability to blast predators with a pungent spray from its anal glands — which animal?
Skunk are mammals in the family Mephitidae.
Often caused by a lesion narrowing an artery, as in atherosclerosis, this condition is sometimes also called a stricture or coarctation — what is it?
Stenosis (from Ancient Greek (stens) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.
A staple corm across African, Caribbean, Oceanian, and Asian cultures, this root vegetable of the arum family is often likened to yams — what is it?
Taro (Colocasia esculenta) is a root vegetable.

Founding pastor of Redeemer Presbyterian Church in New York City and co-founder of Redeemer City to City, this American theologian wrote the bestsellers The Reason for God and The Prodigal God — who was he?
Tim Keller (pastor) (September 23, 1950 - May 19, 2023) was an American Presbyterian pastor, Reformed theologian, and Christian apologist.
A byproduct of purine breakdown normally found in urine, elevated blood levels of this heterocyclic compound can cause gout and kidney stones — what's the compound (C5H4N4O3)?
Uric acid is a heterocyclic compound of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen with the formula C5H4N4O3.
These big cetaceans — everything in the group except dolphins and porpoises — count the hippopotamus as their closest living relative on land. What are they?
Whale are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Unlike its bulb-forming relative, the common onion, this perennial vegetable never forms a bulb and owes one of its names to its hollow, tube-like leaves — which plant?
Allium fistulosum: Species of plant. The species is very similar in taste and odor to the related common onion, Allium cepa, and hybrids between the two (tree onions) exist.
This Russian physicist miraculously survived a 1978 accident in which a high-energy proton beam from a particle accelerator passed directly through his skull — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski: Soviet and Russian scientist (born 1942)
Most often caused by stroke or head trauma, this condition impairs a person's ability to understand or produce language because specific brain regions aren't working. What is it?
Aphasia: Inability to comprehend or formulate language.
Larger than a meteoroid but smaller than a planet, most of these rocky, metallic, or icy bodies orbit between Mars and Jupiter — what are they called?
Asteroid: Minor planet found within the inner Solar System.
Named by naturalist Constantine Rafinesque in 1815, this predatory saltwater fish prowls near coral reefs and is a favorite target of sport anglers worldwide — what is it?
Split into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism, this scientific field studies the chemical processes that occur within living organisms — which field?

Biochemistry: Study of chemical processes of living organisms. Biochemistry, or biological chemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.
Built as a militarized derivative of a popular 737 airliner, this maritime patrol aircraft hunts submarines for the US Navy and allies like India, Australia and the UK — which aircraft?
Boeing P-8 Poseidon: American maritime patrol aircraft. The Boeing P-8 Poseidon is an American maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft developed and produced by Boeing Defense, Space & Security.

Characterized by cycles of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors like self-induced vomiting, this eating disorder has an estimated genetic risk factor between 30 and 80 percent — what is it called?
Bulimia nervosa: Eating disorder. Bulimia is more common among those who have a close relative with the condition.
Discovered in 1940 and making up as much as 40% of cannabis extract, this compound is an anticonvulsant used to treat two rare forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?

Cannabidiol: Phytocannabinoid discovered in 1940. In the United States, the cannabidiol drug Epidiolex was approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2018, for the treatment of two seizure disorders.
Their young are calves and their castrated males are oxen; this widespread bovid is the most far-flung species of the genus Bos — what animal is it?
Traceable to fairy tales that weren't classified this way until the seventeenth century, this genre spans picture books for toddlers to young-adult fiction for teens — what category of writing?
Children's literature: Stories, books, magazines, and poems primarily written for children.
Sold under the brand name Klonopin, this long-acting benzodiazepine kicks in within an hour and lasts eight to twelve, treating anxiety, seizures, and panic — which drug is it?
Clonazepam: Benzodiazepine medication. It possesses anxiolytic, anticonvulsant, sedative, hypnotic, and skeletal muscle relaxant properties.

Nicknamed the deaf adder or long-cripple in parts of Europe, this legless, burrowing lizard has smooth scales that don't overlap — and despite its name, it's neither a snake nor what it sounds like. What is it?
Common slow worm: Species of legless lizard. The common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.
Stalked ones anchored to the seafloor are nicknamed 'sea lilies' while the free-swimming kind are 'feather stars' — what's the class name for these mouth-on-top echinoderms?
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded and serves as CEO of Roblox Corporation, after his earlier company was acquired by MSC Software in 1998 — who is he?

Cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years despite not being formally described until 1780, this tree produces the most widely grown fruit in its genus, known by names like Japanese or Chinese persimmon. Which species?
Diospyros kaki: Oriental fruit. Although its first botanical description was not published until 1780, D. kaki cultivation in China dates back more than 2000 years.
Known medically as cerumen, this waxy secretion in the ear canal protects against bacteria, fungi, and water while trapping dust and dead skin — what is it?
Earwax: Waxy substance secreted by the ear.

This discipline systematically applies science and math to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft, with traditional branches in civil, mechanical, electrical, and chemical work — which field?
This small finch native to Europe and Asia is the original species to bear its common English name, and goes by 'plum bird' in Shropshire — what is it?
Eurasian bullfinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian bullfinch or common bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.

Marketed under the brand name Captagon, this amphetamine-theophylline combination drug became Syria's largest export under the Assad regime, with tablet stockpiles seized when anti-government forces took Damascus in December 2024. What drug is this?
Fenethylline: Codrug of amphetamine and theophylline. Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.
Named for hindwings that resemble human ears when unfolded, this reddish-brown insect is a common household pest known for the pincers at the tip of its abdomen — which species?
Forficula auricularia: Species of earwig. It is an omnivorous insect belonging to the family Forficulidae.
Nicknamed the 'stomach flu' in the US and Canada, this inflammation of the gut is most often caused in kids by rotavirus and in adults by norovirus — what is it?
Gastroenteritis: Inflammation of the stomach and small intestine.
Produced by the pancreas's alpha cells, this hormone raises blood sugar by triggering the liver to break down stored glycogen — the functional opposite of insulin. What is it?
Glucagon: Peptide hormone. It raises the concentration of glucose and fatty acids in the bloodstream and is considered to be the main catabolic hormone of the body.
Credited as the inventor of radio, this Italian engineer shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics and later set up Vatican Radio for Pope Pius XI — who is he?
Guglielmo Marconi: Italian radio-frequency engineer and inventor (1874–1937)
Native to Africa south of the Sahara, this domesticated bird has since been introduced everywhere from the West Indies to Australia — which species?
Helmeted guinea fowl: Species of bird. The helmeted guinea fowl (Numida meleagris) is the best known of the guinea fowl bird family, Numididae, and the only member of the genus Numida.
Also called the ratel, this remarkably loose-skinned mammal — able to twist freely inside its own hide — is the largest land member of the weasel family in Africa. What is it?
Honey badger: Species of mammal. The honey badger (Mellivora capensis), also known as the ratel ( or), is a mammal widely distributed across Africa, Southwest Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

Diagnosed via Whipple's triad and most often triggered by diabetes medications like insulin, this condition causes shakiness, confusion, and sweating when blood sugar drops below 70 mg/dL — what is it?

Hypoglycemia: Decrease in blood sugar. It is defined as blood glucose below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), symptoms associated with hypoglycemia, and resolution of symptoms when blood sugar returns to normal.
Most often extracted from chicory, this plant-stored fructan earned FDA approval as a dietary fiber in 2018 and remains the gold-standard compound for measuring kidney filtration rates — what is it?
A Communist Party member and Stanford-trained psychiatrist, this woman is best remembered for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer, which put her under FBI surveillance. Who is she?
Personal physician to the Buddha and King Bimbisāra in 5th-century BCE Rājagṛha, this 'Medicine King' is still revered by traditional healers across Asia — who is he?

Jīvaka: Personal physician of the Buddha and Indian King Bimbisara. Jīvaka (Pali: Jīvaka Komārabhacca; Sanskrit: Jīvaka Kaumārabhṛtya) was the personal physician (Sanskrit: vaidya) of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisāra.
What is this — “Parts of the vulva”?
Labia: Parts of the vulva. The labia are the major externally visible structures of the vulva.
This synthetic thyroid hormone treats hypothyroidism, has a half-life of roughly 7.5 days, and is not intended for weight loss — what's this medication?
Levothyroxine: Thyroid hormone medication. Levothyroxine, also known as L-thyroxine, is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4).
Patented in 1980 and marketed as Claritin, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever and hives but can still cause sleepiness and dry mouth — what is it?
Loratadine: Antihistamine medication. Loratadine, sold under the brand name Claritin among others, is a medication used to treat allergies.
Produced when beta-amylase breaks starch down two glucose units at a time, which reducing disaccharide gets its name from the germinating-seed process of malting?

The largest trijet ever built, this American wide-body airliner first flew in January 1990 and entered service with Finnair that December, a stretched, winglet-equipped update of an earlier trijet — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-11: Wide body airliners developed from the DC-10.
A physician-turned-hedge-fund-manager, this investor famously predicted the subprime mortgage crisis and was portrayed in the 2015 film The Big Short — who is he?
Michael Burry: American hedge fund manager (born 1971)
Making up about 23% of all named marine organisms, this phylum is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after the arthropods — what is it?
In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature into healthy ones, and some cases progress into acute myeloid leukemia — what is it called?
Myelodysplastic syndrome: Diverse collection of blood-related cancers.
Unlike its niacin cousin, this form of vitamin B3 treats pellagra without causing skin flushing, and as a cream is used to fade acne scars and reduce hyperpigmentation — what is it?
This order of predatory flying insects includes dragonflies and damselflies, whose aquatic larvae are voracious carnivores capable of overpowering small fish and tadpoles — what is it called?
Odonata: Order of insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies. The adults are superb aerial hunters and their legs are specialised for catching prey in flight.
Sold under the brand name Anavar, this synthetic anabolic steroid helps burn victims and Turner syndrome patients gain weight — what is it?
Oxandrolone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It was sold under the brand names Oxandrin and Anavar, among others.
Nicknamed the empress tree for its fast growth and showy foxglove-like blooms, which East Asian hardwood has become an invasive species across the Eastern US?
Paulownia tomentosa: Species of deciduous tree classified in its own family.

Approved for medical use in the US back in 1959 and sold under the brand name Adipex-P, this appetite-suppressing stimulant is a substituted amphetamine used alongside diet and exercise to treat obesity — what is it?

There are exactly five of these convex regular polyhedra — tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron — named for the philosopher who linked them to the classical elements. What are they called?
Platonic solid: Any of the five regular polyhedra. In geometry, a Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.

A trained engineer by profession, this royal consort married King Mohammed VI in 2002, becoming the first publicly acknowledged wife of a reigning monarch there to hold an official title, before their discreet 2018 divorce. Who is she?
Princess Lalla Salma of Morocco: Moroccan royal (born 1978)
Imagine a benzene ring with one CH swapped for a nitrogen atom: the result is this flammable, fish-smelling liquid once distilled from coal tar and now made at 20,000 tons a year — what is it?
Known in North America as caribou, this circumpolar deer species ranges from the tiny Svalbard subspecies to the much larger Osborn's version roaming the Arctic tundra — which animal is it?
Reindeer: Species of deer. It is the only representative of the genus Rangifer.

This chronic skin condition causes facial redness, small dilated blood vessels, and in severe cases an enlarged red nose, and can be triggered by spicy food, alcohol, or sun exposure — which condition?
Rosacea: Skin condition, usually on the face.
Nicknamed 'mother-in-law's tongue' and 'snake plant,' this genus of stiff, sword-leaved succulents from Africa and southern Asia is now classified within Dracaena — which genus?
Serving as mayor of Moscow since 2010, this Russian politician previously headed the presidential administration and served as a deputy prime minister under Vladimir Putin — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin: Mayor of Moscow since 2010. At the same time, Sobyanin was criticized for the banning of pride parades in the city, for which he was strongly condemned by LGBT groups.
This big cat of the genus Panthera prowls the alpine zones of Central and South Asia at elevations of 3,000 to 4,500 meters, from the Himalayas to southern Siberia — what is it?
Snow leopard: Species of large felid.

First recognized as a distinct breed by the UK Kennel Club in 1935, this purebred originated in 19th-century Birmingham from crosses of bulldogs with various other breeds developed for close combat — what breed is it?
Staffordshire Bull Terrier: British breed of dog.
